start.text: Abuja. Federal Capital Territory. Wide roads, big gates, bigger dreams. You are nine years old.

home_lapo.speaker: Mama
home_lapo.text: One room in Nyanya. Mama sells pepper and tomatoes by the junction. Last night, garri without sugar again. This morning she says: "{name}, after school, come help me for the stall o."

choices.text: Help Mama at the stall every day
choices.result: You learn to count change faster than your teacher. Your homework suffers small.

choices.text: Beg to focus on your books
choices.result: Mama sighs, but she lets you read under the one bulb. When NEPA allows.

fees.speaker: Headmaster
fees.text: Assembly. The headmaster reads names. Yours is on the list. "Those owing school fees, go home and come back with your parents." The whole school turns to look.

choices.text: Sell sachet water at the junction with Tunde

remember.what: You sold pure water with them at the junction as kids
remember.say: "You remember when we used to sell pure water at the junction? Two of us, shouting 'Pure wa-ter!' Hustle started early."

effects.log: Sold pure water at nine to help pay school fees.

choices.result: Tunde shows you the best spot: under the bridge, where the danfo drivers stop. By Friday, half the fees are paid.
Uncle Sylvester gives a long speech about 'hard work' and ₦500. He will remind the family of this ₦500 for the next twenty years.

choices.text: Stay home and study from a borrowed textbook
choices.result: You miss two weeks of school, but you finish the borrowed textbook. Twice.

home_average.speaker: Daddy
home_average.text: A two-bedroom flat in Gwarinpa. Daddy is a civil servant at the Federal Secretariat; Mummy trades fabrics in Wuse Market. Not rich, not suffering. Daddy says: "{name}, this term, I want to see results."

choices.result: The lesson teacher smells of Robb and wisdom. Your maths improves.

choices.text: Help Mummy at her fabric stall on Saturdays
choices.result: You learn that every customer says "last price" and nobody means it.
You are not Okocha, but the whole estate knows your name.

friends.text: Break time. Tunde, the boy who always comes early because his mama opens shop at 6, sits alone with nothing to eat. Slim, the boy with new shoes every term, waves you over: "My guy, copy my homework. I get the answers."

remember.what: You shared your lunch with them when they had nothing
remember.say: "I still think about that time you shared your lunch with me. Nobody else did. I never forgot."

effects.log: Shared lunch with Tunde. He never forgot.

choices.result: Tunde splits your bread exactly in half. "I go pay you back one day," he says. He means it.

remember.what: You copied their homework in primary school
remember.say: "Primary school, you were copying my homework. Now look at us. I'm still the brains, sha."

choices.result: Full marks, zero learning. Slim winks: "Stick with me."
Tunde brings the jokes, Slim brings the gist. You bring yourself.

end.text: Primary school ends. Your mother cries at the graduation. Your father pretends he is not crying. Somewhere in Maitama, a boy your age has just been given his first car keys. For when he turns sixteen.

sweets.speaker: Mrs. Bassey
sweets.text: Your class is a market. Kemi sells Tom-Tom at ₦10, Musa sells chin-chin in nylon, and somebody is renting out a Game Boy by the minute. Mrs. Bassey, the class teacher, has banned trading in class. Everybody trades in class.

choices.text: Buy sweets in bulk at the junction and sell them in class

then.toast: Mrs. Bassey seizes your whole stock and eats a Tom-Tom in front of you.

else.toast: Sold out by second period. ₦1,200 profit.

choices.result: Buy low, sell at break. Simple economics. Mostly.

choices.text: Become the class monitor who writes the names of noisemakers
choices.result: Chalk, a ruler and power. Your classmates start being very nice to you.

choices.text: Collect ₦200 each for a 'class party'… that nobody planned

remember.what: You collected fake party money from the class
remember.say: "You remember that 'class party' money? Some people still talk about it."

then.toast: Somebody's mother calls the school. There is no party. There is you, in the headmaster's office.

choices.result: Twenty classmates, ₦200 each. The party is always 'next Friday'.

choices.text: Stay out of it and read
choices.result: Your exercise book is the neatest in class. Nobody buys anything from you.

interhouse.speaker: Games master
interhouse.text: Inter-house sports week! The whole school is split into four houses. There are march-pasts, drummers, parents on plastic chairs, and a trophy that the headmaster polishes every morning. Which house are you in?

choices.result: Red vest, red ribbon, red face paint. Your house captain hugs you like you have already won.
Blue House: the house of serious people and loud drummers.
Green House. The colour of the flag, the colour of victory, says your house master.
Yellow House. Bright vests, brighter mouths. Your house sings the loudest.

interhouse_events.text: The pitch is chalked, the drummers are going, and your house captain needs points. Pick your event.

game.winText: You burst through the tape! Your house mates carry you on their shoulders.
game.loseText: Fourth. Your legs had other plans.

game.winText: Hop, hop, hop, WIN! Nobody has ever been so proud of a rice sack.
game.loseText: You fall flat in your sack. The parents laugh. Kindly.

choices.text: Carry the egg in the egg-and-spoon race

game.winText: Not a crack! Your house cheers like you've scored at the World Cup.
game.loseText: Splat. The egg is everywhere. Your sports vest smells for a week.

choices.text: Put a stone in the shoe of Slim's house runner

remember.what: You sabotaged their house runner
remember.say: "I know it was you who put that stone in our runner's shoe."

then.toast: The runner shows the stone to the games master. Everyone looks at you.

else.toast: Their runner limps home last. Your house gets the point. Your conscience does not.

choices.result: You find a small, sharp stone.

choices.text: Sell zobo and puff-puff to the parents
choices.result: Hot sun plus thirsty parents equals ₦2,500. You learn the first law of business.

interhouse_events2.text: Last event of the day: tug of war, house against house. Your captain counts the strongest children twice.

choices.text: Anchor the rope for your house

game.winText: The rope slides your way, inch by inch… and over the line! Tunde jumps on your back.
game.loseText: Your house ends up in the sand. Together, at least.

choices.text: Lead the march-past with the house flag
choices.result: Left, right, left. You salute the headmaster like a general. Best march-past: your house.
You lose your voice. You gain a reputation for noise.

interhouse_tourney.speaker: Games master
interhouse_tourney.text: One more thing before the trophy: the inter-house football tournament. Four houses, knockout, and because the pitch is only half a pitch, every match is settled by penalties. {house} plays {semi_rival} in the semi-final.

game.winText: Your last kick hits the net and {house} is through to the final! The drummers go mad.
game.loseText: {semi_rival} win it. Your house captain pats your back. There's still third place to play for.

choices.result: You drum on a paint bucket until your hands hurt. Your house still calls you a hero.

interhouse_tourney_final.speaker: Games master
interhouse_tourney_final.text: The final: {house} against {final_rival}. Parents have climbed onto the classroom windows to watch, and the headmaster has taken off his jacket.

win.log: Won the inter-house football tournament in primary school.

remember.what: You won the inter-house football final together
remember.say: "That penalty in the primary school final! I still dream about it."

game.winText: The keeper dives the wrong way and the ball rolls in. {house} win the football cup! Tunde runs the length of the pitch with his shirt over his head.
game.loseText: So close. {final_rival} take the cup, but your house claps you off the pitch.

interhouse_tourney_third.speaker: Games master
interhouse_tourney_third.text: The match for third place: {house} against {third_rival}. Smaller crowd, same nerves.

game.winText: Bronze! Third place goes to {house}, and the medals are made of real tin.
game.loseText: Fourth place. The games master says you all played 'with spirit'.

interhouse_tourney_done.text: The football tournament is over. Here's how it finished.

interhouse_end.text: The headmaster lifts the trophy. The results are read out.

interhouse_cup.text: "And the overall winner of this year's inter-house sports is…" Your house. The trophy goes up, the drummers lose their minds, and for one afternoon you are famous.

effects.log: Won the inter-house sports cup in primary school.

remember.what: You won the inter-house cup together
remember.say: "Primary school inter-house! You remember how we carried that trophy?"

interhouse_close.text: Your house doesn't win the cup this year. The winners dance past your stand. Your house master says, "Next year," like he says every year.

common_entrance.text: Common Entrance is next month: the exam into secondary school. A man at the junction runs a 'special centre' where, they say, the answers are written on the board.

choices.text: Study with past questions every evening
choices.result: Your Mama tests you every night by the lantern. You know your times tables in your sleep.

then.toast: Exam officials raid the centre. Your name is on their list.

else.toast: The answers really are on the board. You pass. You learn nothing.

choices.result: A crowded room, a man with chalk, and a lookout at the door.

remember.what: You helped them study for Common Entrance
remember.say: "I passed Common Entrance because you drilled me. Don't think I forgot."

choices.result: Two heads, one lantern. Both of you pass.

suspended.speaker: Headmaster
suspended.text: "You are suspended for two weeks." The headmaster writes a letter for your parents. The walk home is the longest of your life.

choices.text: Help at the stall while you're home
choices.result: Two weeks of selling tomatoes and hearing about it from every customer.

choices.text: Study at home and promise to change
choices.result: You copy your notes twice. The promise is real, mostly.

choices.text: Roam the street with the older boys
choices.result: They teach you things that are not in the curriculum.

expelled.speaker: Headmaster
expelled.text: "Pack your things. You are no longer a pupil of this school." Your parents are called in. Mama cries; Daddy does not speak for three days.

choices.text: Start again at a cheaper school across town

remember.what: You got expelled and moved schools

effects.log: Expelled from primary school and moved to another.

choices.result: New uniform, new teachers, same you. You decide which version.

choices.text: Beg the headmaster with a 'development levy' (₦10,000)
choices.result: Daddy pays. The headmaster finds that he can forgive you after all.

crush_note.text: At break, {pcrush} from your class keeps looking at your desk, then looking away. Tunde says it's obvious. Kemi says it's "very obvious".

choices.text: Write a note: "Do you like me? Tick Yes or No"

remember.what: You sent them a love note in primary school
remember.say: "I still have that note you wrote me. 'Tick Yes or No.' I ticked Yes."

then.toast: The note comes back folded small. 'Yes' is ticked, twice.

else.toast: The note comes back with 'Maybe' written in. You will think about 'Maybe' for a week.

choices.result: You fold it into a tiny square and pass it along the row.

choices.text: Ask {pcrush} to walk round the school with you at break
choices.result: Round the classroom block, past the headmaster's office, back again. You talk about cartoons the whole time.
{pcrush} takes the biggest one. You let them.

choices.text: Too shy. Pretend you haven't noticed
choices.result: You stare at your exercise book so hard you nearly read it.

prefects_primary.text: End of term. The teachers meet in the staff room and choose next year's prefects. The list goes up on the notice board on Monday.

prefect_p_head.speaker: Headmaster
prefect_p_head.text: Your name is at the top of the list: {headrole}! The headmaster pins the badge on you at assembly. Mama wears her best wrapper to watch.

effects.log: Became {headrole} in primary school.

choices.result: Every morning you stand in front of the whole school. Nobody looks at your shoes; they look at your badge.

choices.text: Use the badge to write your enemies' names as 'noisemakers'

then.toast: A teacher notices the same three names every single day.

choices.result: Power. Small power, but power.

choices.text: Skip the queue at Mama Put with your badge
choices.result: Rank has privileges. The queue has opinions.

prefect_p_sports.speaker: Games master
prefect_p_sports.text: The games master chose you as Sports Prefect, after what you did on sports day. You get a whistle. You will never put it down.

choices.text: Train the class for next year's sports

effects.log: Became Sports Prefect in primary school.

choices.result: Laps before assembly. Everyone hates you for a week, then they win.

choices.text: Pick only your friends for the team
choices.result: Tunde is in. Tunde is always in.

prefect_p_captain.speaker: Mrs. Bassey
prefect_p_captain.text: Mrs. Bassey makes you Class Captain: you keep the class quiet and write the names of noisemakers on the board.

choices.text: Be fair, even to your friends

effects.log: Became Class Captain in primary school.

choices.result: You write Tunde's name once. He forgives you. Eventually.

choices.text: Take sweets to leave names off the list

then.toast: Somebody who didn't pay reports you.

choices.result: Tom-Tom is the currency of justice.

prefect_p_labour.text: The teachers make you Labour Prefect: you supervise the Friday cleaning and the grass-cutting. They noticed you work hard.

effects.log: Became Labour Prefect in primary school.

choices.result: Even the headmaster's office shines.

choices.text: Make the small ones do your share

then.toast: A Primary 2 pupil cries to the headmaster.

choices.result: Leadership is delegation, you tell yourself.

prefect_none_bad.text: Your name isn't on the list. "With your record?" a teacher says, not quietly enough.

prefect_none.text: Your name isn't on the prefects' list this year. You get to ring the bell on Fridays, which, honestly, is the best job in the school.

start.text: Secondary school. New uniform (yours is your cousin's old one, if you are a Lapo Baby; new from the tailor if not). Same Tunde. Same Slim. New problems.

lapo_school.text: Community secondary school, Nyanya. Forty-eight students per class, one fan, no NEPA. The chemistry lab is a picture of a chemistry lab. But the teachers who care, really care.

choices.result: Your argument that 'NEPA should be renamed Never Expect Power Always' wins the inter-school round.

choices.text: Run errands for traders after school
choices.result: Small money, steady money. Your schoolbag smells like crayfish.

average_school.text: Federal Government College. Boarding school. Senior students who think they are the Army. The food is a crime scene, but the teachers are decent and the alumni network is long.

choices.result: You build a robot from a biscuit tin. It moves forward, once.

choices.text: Become the class 'provost' who sells provisions
choices.result: Indomie at ₦50 profit per pack. You are the Dangote of Hostel B.

big_event.speaker: Bolaji
big_event.text: Inter-school quiz at a 'big' school in Maitama. A convoy rolls in: two Prados, one siren. Out steps Bolaji Danjuma-Adeyemi, son of (fictional) Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi. He scans your team. "You guys came by bus? Respect, honestly."

remember.what: You introduced yourself at school, no fear
remember.say: "You were the only one in that school who talked to me like a normal person. Not my father's son. Me."

effects.log: Met Bolaji, a Nepo Baby, at a quiz in Maitama.

choices.result: He gives you his number. And his driver's number, 'in case'.

choices.text: Beat his team in the quiz

effects.log: Beat the Maitama school in a quiz. Bolaji clapped.

choices.result: You win. Bolaji claps, genuinely. His father's aide does not.
Pride is free. For now.

peer.speaker: Slim
peer.text: Slim finds you after school. New iPhone, school shirt untucked. "My guy, there's this runs. You just go collect package for one oga for Lugbe, bring am come. ₦10k per trip. No questions."

remember.what: You did runs for them in secondary school
remember.say: "You did those runs for me back in school and never talked. That kind of loyalty, I remember."

effects.log: Did 'no questions' runs for Slim at fifteen.

choices.result: Two trips, ₦20k. The second package was heavier. You did not ask.

remember.what: You told them the truth about Slim's runs
remember.say: "You told me the truth about Slim back then, when it would have been easier to keep quiet."

remember.what: You snitched to Tunde about their runs
remember.say: "I haven't forgotten you went and told Tunde my business back in school. Water under the bridge… mostly."

choices.result: Tunde says, "Guy, that one na trouble." Slim calls you 'Pastor' for a month.

socials.text: Everyone is on Tiklok now. Your classmate's skit about Nigerian mothers and slippers has 300k views. You open the app.

choices.result: Your third video ("POV: NEPA takes light during WAEC revision") gets 40k views. You understand the algorithm a little.
Four hours vanish. You learn nothing. It was lovely.

crush.text: There is someone in SS2 who laughs at your jokes. Innocent butterflies. You consider writing a note.

choices.result: They reply: "You're funny." You re-read it 400 times.
Love can wait. WAEC cannot.

choices.text: Ask {scrush} to hang out on Saturday

remember.what: They asked you out in secondary school

then.toast: {scrush} says yes. Then pretends it's no big deal.

else.toast: "Maybe after WAEC." Ouch.

choices.result: You catch {scrush} after class, words in a heap.

waec.text: WAEC season. 'Expo' is selling on WhatsApp: ₦5,000 for 'verified' answers. Half the class has bought it.

then.toast: WAEC: 5 credits including Maths and English!

else.toast: WAEC: Maths missed by one mark.

choices.result: You read by candlelight. Results come out.

then.toast: The expo was real. Somehow.

else.toast: The expo was for last year's paper. Of course.

choices.result: You pay. You pray.

then.toast: WAEC: all credits. You didn't write half of them.

else.toast: WAEC cancels the whole centre's results.

choices.result: Answers whispered through the window, a supervisor who looks away.

dropout.text: End of secondary school. Money is tight; university will cost. Some people your age are already making money in the market, on the road, online.

choices.text: Resit WAEC next year, then JAMB

effects.log: Resat WAEC and passed.

choices.result: One more year, one more try. This time, you pass.

choices.text: Drop out and start hustling now

effects.log: Dropped out after secondary school to hustle.

jamb.text: JAMB day. The CBT centre in Garki has three working computers and four hundred candidates.

then.toast: Admission: University of Abuja!

else.toast: Missed the cut-off. Tried again next year and got in.

choices.result: Results drop at midnight. Your phone shakes in your hand.

hustle_hostel.text: Money is moving in this school, and none of it is yours yet. Phones need charging, juniors need help, and everybody is hungry after prep.

choices.text: Run a phone-charging point from the staff room socket (₦100 a charge)

then.toast: The bursar finds your extension box. Confiscated, with a warning.

choices.result: Ten phones a night, ₦100 each. The staff room has never been so popular.

choices.text: Teach JSS1 maths after prep (₦500 a week each)
choices.result: The juniors call you 'Teacher'. Their parents pay on time.

choices.text: Sell Indomie and Milo at 'hostel prices'
choices.result: Buy at the market, sell at midnight. Demand is infinite after lights out.

choices.text: Write love letters for SS1 boys (₦200 a letter)
choices.result: "My heart beats for you like Mama's pestle." Business is booming.

choices.text: Forge exeat slips for students who want to sneak out (₦1,000 each)

then.toast: A forged exeat is found on a student at the bus stop. It has your handwriting.

choices.result: The principal's signature is easy once you've practised it fifty times.

senior.speaker: Senior Chuka
senior.text: Senior Chuka and his 'squad' run the junior block. Every junior pays a 'protection fee'. Today Chuka is standing in front of you, holding out his hand.

choices.result: He pockets it without looking. Next week, he'll be back.

then.toast: Chuka finds out who reported him. Your shin finds out too.

else.toast: Chuka is suspended. The junior block breathes again.

choices.result: You knock on the principal's door, heart pounding.

choices.text: Join his squad and collect from the JSS1s

remember.what: You bullied juniors for money in secondary school
remember.say: "You used to collect 'protection' from the small boys. I didn't like that version of you."

then.toast: A JSS1's father turns out to be a police officer. The principal is not amused.

choices.result: The JSS1s look at you the way you used to look at Chuka.

then.toast: Chuka blinks first. Word spreads: you are not to be touched.

else.toast: It does not go well. But Chuka never asks you again.

choices.result: "No."

interhouse_sec.speaker: Sports master
interhouse_sec.text: Inter-house sports, secondary school edition: real tracks, starting blocks, and the principal in sunglasses. Houses are drawn at random. Which colour are you this time?

choices.result: Red vest, red ribbon, red face paint. Your house captain hugs you like you have already won.
Blue House: the house of serious people and loud drummers.
Green House. The colour of the flag, the colour of victory, says your house master.
Yellow House. Bright vests, brighter mouths. Your house sings the loudest.

interhouse_sec_events.text: Day one on the track. Your house captain has your name against an event.

game.winText: Clean passes, fast legs: your relay team wins it by a stride!
game.loseText: A dropped baton on the third leg. The whole house groans.

game.winText: You lean at the line and take it by a chest!

choices.text: Slip the timekeeper ₦2,000 to 'adjust' your house's times

then.toast: The timekeeper panics and confesses to the sports master. Your name comes up.

else.toast: Your house's times look suspiciously good.

choices.result: You fold the notes small.

choices.text: Sell cold drinks and gala to the crowd
choices.result: A cooler, ice from the kitchen and a loud voice. ₦6,000.

interhouse_sec_events2.text: Day two. The field events and the old favourites.

choices.text: Pull in the tug of war final

game.winText: Your house heaves together and drags them over the line!
game.loseText: They were heavier. They were also louder. You land in the sand.

choices.text: Win the egg-and-spoon for your house's juniors

game.winText: Steady hands. The egg crosses the line unbroken.
game.loseText: The egg goes one way. You go the other.

game.winText: You show the juniors how it's done, and win!
game.loseText: The juniors laugh at you. Then with you.

interhouse_sec_tourney.speaker: Sports master
interhouse_sec_tourney.text: The event the whole school actually cares about: inter-house football. Four houses, knockout, penalties to decide every match because the principal says the grass 'cannot take ninety minutes'. {house} faces {semi_rival} in the semi-final.

game.winText: Top corner. {house} is in the final and the seniors are already composing songs.
game.loseText: {semi_rival} go through. You'll play for third place.

choices.result: You lead the singing from the stands. Your whole house loses its voice.

interhouse_sec_tourney_final.speaker: Sports master
interhouse_sec_tourney_final.text: The final: {house} against {final_rival}. The principal is in sunglasses on the touchline, the drummers have come from the town, and someone is selling meat pies at the gate.

win.log: Won the inter-house football tournament in secondary school.

remember.what: You won the secondary school football final
remember.say: "Inter-house final in secondary school. Top corner! Nobody can take that from you."

game.winText: You keep your nerve and {house} lift the inter-house football cup! The video is on every class WhatsApp group by evening.
game.loseText: {final_rival} win it on the last kick. Runners-up medals and a long walk back to the hostel.

interhouse_sec_tourney_third.speaker: Sports master
interhouse_sec_tourney_third.text: Third place: {house} against {third_rival}. Pride is on the line.

game.winText: Third place for {house}. Bronze, and bragging rights over {third_rival} for a whole term.
game.loseText: Fourth. The seniors say nothing, which is worse than shouting.

interhouse_sec_tourney_done.text: The football tournament is over. The final table goes up on the notice board.

interhouse_sec_end.text: Closing ceremony. Medals, march-past, and the points table on the board.

interhouse_sec_cup.text: Your house wins the cup! The principal shakes your hand. Somebody films the celebration and it goes round every class WhatsApp group.

effects.log: Won the inter-house sports cup in secondary school.

interhouse_sec_close.text: Your house finishes off the podium. Your house master gives a speech about 'character'. Everybody knows what that means.

expo_market.speaker: Slim
expo_market.text: WAEC is weeks away and the expo trade is in full swing. Slim has 'the plug': answers that arrive on WhatsApp the night before each paper. He wants agents.

choices.text: Become an expo agent and resell to your class (₦2,000 a paper)

remember.what: You sold expo for them in secondary school

then.toast: WAEC officials trace the answers to your phone. The principal has the screenshots.

choices.result: Every night, a new PDF. Every morning, a queue at your bunk.

choices.text: Register at a 'miracle centre' for WAEC (₦15,000)
choices.result: The centre promises 'special assistance' in the exam hall. You don't ask what that means.

choices.text: Report the expo ring to the principal

remember.what: You reported their expo business
remember.say: "You snitched on my expo business. I remember."

choices.result: The principal thanks you. Slim does not.
Past questions, a torchlight and stubbornness.

suspended.speaker: Principal
suspended.text: "Two weeks' suspension, and your parents must come and see me." You carry your box out through the gate while the whole class watches from the windows.

choices.text: Work at the market while you're home
choices.result: Two weeks carrying loads in Wuse Market. You come back with money and sore shoulders.

choices.text: Study hard and write an apology letter
choices.result: The principal reads the letter twice. Something in his face softens.
The corner boys have a lot of free time and a lot of ideas.

expelled.speaker: Principal
expelled.text: "You are hereby expelled." The letter is on school paper, with a stamp. Your parents read it twice. WAEC is still ahead of you, but not at this school.

choices.text: Write WAEC as a private candidate (₦25,000)

effects.log: Expelled from secondary school; wrote WAEC privately.

choices.result: Lesson centre by day, past questions by night.

effects.log: Expelled from secondary school; went to a miracle centre for WAEC.

choices.result: Cheaper, faster, and very illegal.

choices.text: Forget school and start hustling now

effects.log: Expelled from secondary school and started hustling.

choices.result: You fold your uniform for the last time.

date.speaker: {scrush}
date.text: Saturday. {scrush} said yes to hanging out. Their parents are strict about getting home early; yours expect you back by seven.

choices.text: Watch a film at Jabi Lake Mall (₦3,000)
choices.result: Popcorn, a loud film and an armrest negotiation.

choices.text: Suya and a walk by the lake (₦1,000)
choices.result: Smoky suya, cold zobo and the lake turning orange.

choices.text: A study date at the library
choices.result: More laughing than studying, but it counts.

date_late.text: It's getting dark. {scrush} checks the time. Some of your friends have a curfew; some don't. Tonight you have to decide whose rules count.

choices.result: Their mother is at the gate, watch in hand. You're two minutes early. She almost smiles.

choices.text: Stay out longer and break the curfew together

then.toast: Caught! {scrush} is grounded for a month, and your own parents hear about it.

choices.result: Ten more minutes becomes an hour.

choices.text: Walk around until late (no curfew tonight)
choices.result: The streets are quiet. You talk about everything.

choices.text: Sneak back past your own curfew

then.toast: The house master is waiting with a torch.

choices.result: Shoes in hand, heart in mouth.

kiss_moment.text: Behind the school block, {scrush} goes quiet and looks at you. Kissing on school grounds gets students suspended. Everybody knows that.

then.toast: A prefect's torch. By Monday the principal knows, and so does everyone else.

remember.what: Your first kiss, behind the school block
remember.say: "Do you remember behind the school block? I was so nervous."

choices.result: A quick, nervous first kiss.
Their hand is warm. You don't wash yours for a day.
"See you Monday." "See you Monday."

prefect_campaign.speaker: Principal
prefect_campaign.text: Prefect elections! Students vote and the teachers confirm. Posts are open for {headrole}, Food Prefect, Sports Prefect, Labour Prefect, Library Prefect, Chapel and Mosque Prefect and Social Prefect.

choices.text: Run for Chapel and Mosque Prefect
Don't run: vote and stay out of politics
choices.result: You vote for whoever promises the best food.

campaign.text: Campaign week. Posters on every wall, promises in every corridor. What's your strategy?

then.toast: The juniors cheer. Even the seniors clap.

else.toast: You forget your second point. People clap politely.

choices.result: You stand in front of the whole school with a sheet of paper and shaking knees.
Your face, in colour, on every notice board.

choices.text: Share biscuits and sachet water to voters (₦4,000)

then.toast: The electoral committee hears about the biscuits.

choices.result: "Vote wisely," you say, handing out Gala.

choices.text: Get Tunde and Slim to campaign for you
choices.result: Tunde knocks on every door. Slim 'reminds' people.

campaign2.text: Debate day in the hall. Your opponent has a microphone, a manifesto and a cousin in SS3.

then.toast: You win the debate on points.

else.toast: Your opponent's jokes land better.

choices.result: Facts, calm, and one good line.

choices.text: Spread a rumour about your opponent

else.toast: The rumour is traced back to you.

choices.result: "Did you hear what they did in JSS2?"
The crowd goes wild. You have no way of delivering this.
The juniors chant your name. Senior Chuka glares.

election.text: Counting day. The ballot box is opened in front of the whole school.

election_dq.text: "Disqualified for inducing voters." Your name is crossed out on the board in red marker.

choices.text: Walk out with your head down

election_lost.text: You lose. Your opponent's promise of free jollof on Fridays was, apparently, more convincing.

won_head.speaker: Principal
won_head.text: You won! You're the new {headrole}. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

effects.log: Elected {headrole} in secondary school.

choices.result: Students start calling you 'Senior' with respect, not fear.

choices.text: Use the post to punish your enemies

effects.log: Elected {headrole} in secondary school.

then.toast: The principal notices you only ever punish Slim's friends.

choices.result: Detention lists, written in your handwriting.

choices.text: Take 'settlement' from latecomers to leave their names out

effects.log: Elected {headrole} in secondary school.

then.toast: A latecomer's father is on the PTA.

choices.result: ₦200 at the gate. Every morning.

won_food.speaker: Principal
won_food.text: You won! You're the new Food Prefect. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

choices.text: Serve fair portions, even to juniors

effects.log: Elected Food Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: The juniors call you 'the fair one'. The seniors call you other things.

choices.text: Skim provisions from the store and sell them

effects.log: Elected Food Prefect in secondary school.

then.toast: The matron counts the Milo tins. You pay back double and lose your badge.

choices.result: Two tins of Milo here, a bag of sugar there.

effects.log: Elected Food Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: Tunde has never been so loyal.

won_sports.speaker: Principal
won_sports.text: You won! You're the new Sports Prefect. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

effects.log: Elected Sports Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: Your school wins the inter-school athletics. Your name is on a plaque.

choices.text: Sell the school's sports kits on the side

effects.log: Elected Sports Prefect in secondary school.

then.toast: The games master finds the school's jerseys at Wuse Market.

choices.result: Jerseys, spikes and a whistle you didn't need.

choices.text: Pick only your friends for the team

effects.log: Elected Sports Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: Loyalty over medals.

won_labour.speaker: Principal
won_labour.text: You won! You're the new Labour Prefect. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

effects.log: Elected Labour Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: The school compound has never looked better.

choices.text: Charge juniors to skip cleaning duty

effects.log: Elected Labour Prefect in secondary school.

then.toast: A junior's mother writes to the principal.

choices.result: ₦100 to skip grass-cutting. Demand is high.

won_library.speaker: Principal
won_library.text: You won! You're the new Library Prefect. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

effects.log: Elected Library Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: Twelve members, one fan and a lot of Chimamanda.

effects.log: Elected Library Prefect in secondary school.

then.toast: The librarian finds the 'rental register' in your bag.

choices.result: The school's books, your price list.

won_chapel.speaker: Principal
won_chapel.text: You won! You're the new Chapel and Mosque Prefect. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

effects.log: Elected Chapel and Mosque Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: Your voice leads the hymns. Even the principal sings.

effects.log: Elected Chapel and Mosque Prefect in secondary school.

then.toast: The chaplain counts twice. You pay back double, in front of the whole school.

choices.result: The basket is heavy on Sundays.

won_social.speaker: Principal
won_social.text: You won! You're the new Social Prefect. The principal pins the badge on you in front of the whole school.

effects.log: Elected Social Prefect in secondary school.

choices.result: A DJ, small chops and the principal dancing badly. Legendary.

effects.log: Elected Social Prefect in secondary school.

then.toast: The bursar finds two sets of accounts.

choices.result: ₦1,000 a ticket, ₦500 to the school.

start.text: University of Abuja, Gwagwalada campus. Hostel with eight people in a four-person room. Somebody's mattress is older than you. Freedom smells like burnt noodles.

choices.result: They meet in a classroom with one socket and seventeen extension boxes.

choices.text: Start a hostel hustle selling snacks
choices.result: Gala and Fanta at 2 a.m. You are a public service.
Your CGPA thanks you. Your social life does not.

strike.text: ASUU is on strike. Again. Indefinitely. "Go home, students." Your four-year course is now a five-year course, minimum.

choices.text: Learn to code from free videos
choices.result: Data costs more than food, but by month six you build your first website.

choices.text: Run a POS stand in Gwagwalada
choices.result: Withdrawal charges are a goldmine. You learn the true face of Nigerian banking.

choices.text: Follow Slim to the 'lab' in Lugbe

remember.what: You followed them to the 'lab' in Lugbe
remember.say: "Lugbe days! You followed me to the lab when nobody believed in me."

effects.log: Learned 'the format' in Slim's yahoo lab during an ASUU strike.

choices.result: Ring lights, three laptops, and 'the format'. You make ₦60k in a week. Your stomach turns a little.

cult.text: Strike over. On campus, two groups are recruiting. One wears berets and uses words like 'protection'. The other is the Rotaract club, which mostly does fundraisers.

then.toast: A rival group attacks. You spend two weeks in the clinic.

then.log: Joined a campus cult. Got hurt for it.

choices.result: Initiation is not a party. It is a lesson in how fast bad decisions get serious.
You organise a charity football match. Even the VC shows up.

mentor.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
mentor.text: Mrs. Okafor, your economics lecturer, stops you after class. "You ask good questions. My consultancy needs an intern this holiday. Unpaid. You will work hard. You will learn plenty."

remember.what: You took their internship at university
remember.say: "I took a chance on you as an intern. Don't make me regret it."

effects.log: Interned with Mrs. Okafor. She became a mentor.

choices.result: You make 300 photocopies and two good impressions. She starts introducing you as 'my person'.
Money now. Maybe doors later. Maybe.

guru.speaker: Prophet Profit
guru.text: Your timeline is full of Prophet Profit, standing beside a Lamborghini (rented). "Forex mentorship: ₦50,000. 95% win rate. Students only discount!"

effects.log: Paid a forex guru ₦50k for a course.

choices.result: The 'course' is four YouTube links and a Telegram group where he sells a second course.

choices.text: Learn trading from free books instead
choices.result: Boring, slow, and actually useful.

nepo_party.speaker: Bolaji
nepo_party.text: Bolaji, now in a private university that charges in dollars, is throwing a party in Maitama. He invites you, if you know him. If you do not, the caterer is hiring waiters for ₦15k a night.

choices.result: You spend ₦20k on an outfit to look like you belong. A senator's aide asks what your father does. You meet three people who will matter.

choices.text: Work the party as a waiter
choices.result: You serve jollof to people your age who don't say thank you. One of them tips ₦20k without looking at you.

love.speaker: {love}
love.text: At a friend's birthday, you meet {love}. Sharp, funny, studying law, and completely unimpressed by fake people. (Both of you are over 18.)

remember.what: You talked all night the first time you met
remember.say: "Sometimes I think about that first night we just talked until morning."

effects.log: Met {love} at a birthday party.

choices.result: You walk them to the gate at 2 a.m. and forget your own name on the way back.

final.text: Final year. Project, defence, and one lecturer who 'cannot find' your file. Some classmates are dropping out to chase money.

effects.log: Graduated from the University of Abuja.

choices.result: Second Class Upper. Your mother tells the whole street.

effects.log: Dropped out of university.

hustle_uni.text: Back on campus. Your allowance won't last the month, and everyone in the hostel has a side hustle.

choices.text: Typing and printing business in the hostel (₦150 a page)
choices.result: One second-hand printer, one extension cord, and every final-year student's project.

choices.text: Barbing or braiding in your room
choices.result: Your room becomes a salon. Your roommate charges a 'standing fee'.
You buy in bulk, sell by the gig. Small, steady money.

choices.text: Write assignments and projects for rich kids (₦5,000 each)

then.toast: A lecturer notices three 'different' students writing in your exact style.

choices.result: Your own grades suffer a little. Your bank account doesn't.

choices.text: Be a 'picker' for the Yahoo boys: collect their money at the bank for 10%

then.toast: The bank flags the account. Police at the hostel. 'Bail' costs ₦40,000 and the school hears about it.

choices.result: You walk into banks with other people's names and a straight face.

sorting.speaker: Dr. Ekene's boy
sorting.text: Rumour says Dr. Ekene fails half his class unless you 'sort'. His 'boy' is going round collecting ₦20,000 per student.

then.toast: It's an anti-corruption sting. Your name is on the list of students who paid.

choices.result: You hand over the envelope behind the faculty building.

choices.text: Report it to the anti-corruption desk

then.toast: Dr. Ekene fails you anyway. You carry the course over.

else.toast: Dr. Ekene is suspended pending investigation. Half the class owes you a drink.

choices.result: You write it all down and sign your name.

choices.text: Study harder and take your chances
choices.result: You read his old exam papers until you can predict his questions.

choices.text: Sell fake 'sorting slots' to classmates and keep the money

then.toast: Twenty classmates fail anyway, and all twenty know your room number.

choices.result: If people are paying anyway, why not to you?

ponzi.text: 'Naija Wealth Circle' is all over campus: put in money, get 30% a month. Your roommate's cousin made ₦200,000. There's a WhatsApp group with 4,000 people.

then.toast: It pays! ₦40,000 back. For now.

else.toast: The website goes down. The WhatsApp admin leaves the group. Your ₦20,000 is gone.

choices.result: You click 'Provide Help'.

choices.text: Become an 'upline': recruit classmates for a 10% cut

remember.what: You recruited them into the Ponzi scheme that crashed
remember.say: "I still haven't recovered the money from that your 'Wealth Circle'."

then.toast: The scheme crashes. Your downlines want their money, from you.

choices.result: You post screenshots of 'returns' every hour.

choices.text: Warn people on the class group chat
choices.result: Half the class calls you a hater. The other half thanks you three months later.
You scroll past. Your money stays yours.

yahoo_hostel.speaker: Chairman Tobi
yahoo_hostel.text: Room 14 never sleeps: laptops, ring lights, three phones each. 'Chairman' Tobi corners you. "Format don change. Romance, crypto, billing. You get brain. Join us."

then.toast: EFCC raids the hostel at 3 a.m. Your laptop is in the evidence bag.

choices.result: "Hello dear, I am a US Army doctor on a peacekeeping mission…"

choices.text: Do 'billing' only: chat for them for ₦30,000 a month
choices.result: You type sweet things to strangers in other time zones. It doesn't feel like nothing.

choices.text: Report Room 14 to the hall warden

then.toast: Someone slips a note under your door: 'We know your room.'

choices.result: The warden nods slowly. Too slowly.
You put in your earphones and walk past Room 14 every night.

suspended.speaker: Dean of Students
suspended.text: "Suspended for one semester." Your name is on the notice board. Your classmates will graduate a semester before you.

choices.result: A semester of business. You come back richer and behind.

choices.text: Write an apology and study at home
choices.result: The Dean accepts the letter. Your record keeps the stain.

expelled.speaker: Disciplinary committee
expelled.text: "Rusticated." The disciplinary committee's letter is short. Four years, gone. Outside the senate building, a man in a cap waits for students like you.

choices.text: Buy a degree certificate from 'a connect' in Area 1 (₦150,000)

effects.log: Bought a fake degree certificate after being rusticated.

choices.result: Embossed, signed, 'verifiable'. You pray nobody ever verifies it.

effects.log: Rusticated, then finished at a private university.

choices.result: Dollar fees, air-conditioned classrooms, and a fresh start.

choices.text: Leave school and hustle in Abuja

effects.log: Rusticated from university.

choices.result: No degree, no waiting.

uni_romance.speaker: {love}
uni_romance.text: {love} and you are inseparable this semester. (You're both adults now; the hostel rules are not.) Overnight guests are banned, and the porters do room checks.

choices.result: Shawarma in Wuse 2, live music at a lounge, a long ride home.

choices.text: Rent a room off campus together (₦30,000)
choices.result: A self-contain with a fridge that works some days. It's yours.

choices.text: Sneak {love} into your hostel room for the night

then.toast: The porter does a room check at 2 a.m. Your name goes to the Dean of Students.

choices.result: You sign them in as your 'cousin'. The rest of the night stays between the two of you.
Long phone calls and longer walks.

uni_romance2.text: Final year. {love} wants to spend the weekend with you before exams swallow you both.

choices.text: Sneak them into the hostel again

then.toast: The porter does a room check at 2 a.m. Your name goes to the Dean of Students.

choices.result: Same porter. Same 'cousin'. You hope.

choices.text: Book a hotel room off campus (₦20,000)
choices.result: Room service, no porters, no rules.
"After exams," you promise.

start.text: Your call-up letter drops. One year of national service. Without the NYSC certificate, most government and big corporate jobs will lock you out. With it, you will spend a year being called 'Corper'.

effects.log: Skipped NYSC.

choices.result: Freedom now. Paperwork problems later.

camp.text: Orientation camp, Kubwa. Registration queues, white shorts, white canvas, and a soldier screaming "Corper, double up!" at 4:30 a.m. You swear the oath with two thousand other corpers. Three weeks start now.

choices.result: You become your platoon's leader. Everyone knows your name by day three.

choices.text: Keep your head down and save energy
choices.result: You perfect the art of looking busy while doing nothing.

activities.text: Afternoons are for camp activities. The SAED tents teach skills you can earn from. The Man O' War team runs obstacle courses. The cultural troupe practises dances from every state.

choices.text: SAED: learn ICT and web design
choices.result: Two weeks of HTML, Excel and a certificate from a man who calls computers 'the system'. It's a start.

choices.text: SAED: learn fashion design or catering
choices.result: You leave with a skill people will always pay for.

choices.text: Join the Man O' War drills
choices.result: Rope climbs, mud crawls, river crossings. You come out tougher.
You learn three dances and thirty new friends.

lecture1.speaker: Camp Commandant
lecture1.text: 8 a.m. lecture in the hall: "The NYSC Act, national unity and your duties as a corps member." Attendance will be taken. Officials walk the hostels looking for anyone hiding.

choices.result: Long, hot and slow. But your name is on the attendance list.

then.toast: A soldier finds you under your mattress. Punishment: frog jumps round the parade ground, then cutting grass in the sun until 2 p.m.

else.toast: Nobody checks your hostel. You sleep like a baby. But your name is missing from the attendance list.

games.text: Sports week and social nights. The inter-platoon football final is on Saturday, the volleyball courts are busy, and Friday night is the Mr and Miss NYSC pageant and talent show.

choices.text: Play in the platoon football final

then.toast: You score the winner in the 89th minute. Your platoon carries you round the field. Legend.

else.toast: You lose on penalties. Platoon 4 will never let you forget it.

then.toast: You're crowned! ₦20,000 prize money and a sash you will keep forever.

else.toast: First runner-up. The crowd loved you anyway.

then.toast: Your performance goes viral on camp WhatsApp. Two thousand new fans.

else.toast: The microphone dies halfway through. People still laugh about it. Not with you.

choices.text: Tug of war and volleyball, just for fun
choices.result: No trophies, lots of laughs.

choices.text: Anchor your platoon in the tug-of-war final

win.log: Won the NYSC camp tug-of-war final.

game.winText: Your platoon drags them over the line! The commandant shakes your hand.
game.loseText: The other platoon was all Man O' War boys. You land in a heap.

lecture2.speaker: SAED Director
lecture2.text: Final week lecture: "Entrepreneurship, business loans and life after service", with a bank manager and a successful ex-corper. Missing lectures twice can delay your certificate.

choices.result: The ex-corper gives you her card. "Call me when you start something."

then.toast: Caught with suya in your hand. You spend the evening scrubbing the camp kitchen pots.

else.toast: You get away with it. The suya was worth it. Your attendance record disagrees.

mammy.text: Mammy market at night: fried yam, phone charging for ₦200, and every corps member in Nigeria sharing gist. Someone you met in camp asks you to join their table.

choices.result: New contacts from five states. One of them is starting a logistics business.
One generator, twelve extensions, a business plan.

posting_talk.text: Posting day is close. Rumour says Nepo Baby corpers are already 'confirmed' for Abuja and Lagos. Around camp, fixers whisper that they can keep you in Abuja. For a price.

fixers.text: Behind the camp clinic, the fixers gather. Each one has a reputation, if you know who to ask. Stars shown above their heads come from other corpers' reviews.

choices.text: Walk away and let fate decide

abuja_posting.text: Camp is over and your first allawee lands: ₦77,000. Your posting letter says FCT, Abuja. You exhale. Nearby, a Nepo Baby corper who never came to camp is also posted to Abuja. Of course.

choices.text: Take a PPA at a federal ministry
choices.result: Your job is to carry files from Room 12 to Room 14. Twice a day.

choices.text: Take a PPA at a tech startup in Wuse
choices.result: The startup has a PlayStation and no salaries. You learn plenty.

effects.log: Finished NYSC camp. First allowance: ₦77,000.

away_posting.text: Camp is over and your first allawee lands: ₦77,000. Your posting letter says: {state}. {state_blurb}

effects.log: Finished NYSC camp. First allowance: ₦77,000.

choices.text: Report to your PPA and make the most of it
choices.result: A new place, new food, new people. Eleven months of service start now.

service1.text: Months 1 to 4 of service. Your allawee arrives every month: 4 × ₦77,000 = ₦308,000. Every Thursday is CDS (Community Development Service) with your group. Miss it and your local inspector takes note.

choices.result: Your CDS group paints a primary school and runs a free health check. The community remembers you.

choices.text: Skip CDS and hustle on the side

then.toast: Your Local Government Inspector marks you absent three Thursdays in a row. A query letter follows.

else.toast: Your CDS group covers for you. This time.

choices.result: ₦40,000 extra from your side hustle.

service2.text: Months 5 to 8. Another ₦308,000 of allawee (4 × ₦77,000). Your PPA pays nothing extra, but the allawee is steady. What do you do with it?

choices.result: Garri and groundnut for dinner, but your savings grow.
Owambes, new clothes and suya every weekend. ₦150,000 gone, no regrets. Mostly.

then.toast: Your side business pays off: ₦190,000 back on ₦100,000.

else.toast: It doesn't take off. You get back ₦40,000 of your ₦100,000.

service3.text: Months 9 to 11. The last ₦231,000 of allawee (3 × ₦77,000): twelve payments of ₦77,000 in all, counting camp. Time for final clearance from your Local Government Inspector.

clearance.text: The inspector opens your file and checks your attendance.

extension.speaker: Local Government Inspector
extension.text: "Absent from lectures, absent from CDS. Your service is extended by two months." No allawee for the extra months, and your friends pass out without you.

effects.log: NYSC service extended by two months for absences.

choices.result: Two long months later, your clearance is finally signed.

pass_out.text: Passing out parade. Khaki ironed sharp, certificate in hand. Real life starts now. Abuja is waiting, with its rent, its traffic, and its opportunities.

effects.log: Completed NYSC.

verify.text: Registration day. An official checks every certificate against the universities' lists.

fake_caught.speaker: NYSC official
fake_caught.text: The official looks at your certificate, then at his list, then at you. "This university says you never graduated." Two soldiers move closer.

then.toast: He folds the money into his file. 'Next!'

else.toast: He takes the money and calls the police anyway.

choices.result: You lean in and lower your voice.

choices.text: Run before they call the police

effects.log: Fled NYSC camp when a fake degree was caught.

choices.result: You leave your mattress and your future at the gate.

camp_hustle.text: Camp has a parade ground, a clinic and, most importantly, a market. Corpers have allowance money and nothing to spend it on.

choices.text: Charge phones with a solar panel (₦200 a phone)
choices.result: One panel, twelve sockets, a queue every evening.

choices.text: Sell the liquid soap you made in SAED
choices.result: Lemon-scented, slightly too thick. Sold out in a day.

choices.text: Run a POS point at Mammy market (5% per withdrawal)
choices.result: Everybody wants cash. You are the bank now.

choices.text: Sell fake 'Abuja posting guaranteed' slots to desperate corpers

then.toast: A corper you sold a 'slot' to is the son of an army colonel.

choices.result: "My uncle is in the posting committee." You have no uncle.

choices.text: Bribe a soldier to skip 4:30 a.m. drills (₦2,000)

then.toast: The commandant does a surprise headcount.

choices.result: Sleep is the best investment in camp.

ghost.speaker: Mr. Audu (LGI)
ghost.text: Your Local Government Inspector, Mr. Audu, makes you an offer over tea. "₦10,000 a month and I mark you present. You can stay in Abuja and do your business."

then.toast: A surprise monitoring visit finds your desk empty for the third time.

choices.result: Allowance in one pocket, Abuja hustle in the other.
Mr. Audu shrugs and pours more tea.

then.toast: You're 'redeployed' to the most remote school in the local government.

choices.result: You write to the state coordinator.

cds_funds.text: Your CDS group raised ₦400,000 for a borehole in the village where you serve. You're the treasurer. The contractor winks: "I can write ₦550,000 on the quote. We share the difference."

effects.log: Built a borehole with my CDS group.

choices.result: Clean water on commissioning day. The village chief gives you a title.

then.toast: Your CDS secretary checks the contractor's real price.

choices.result: The borehole works. Mostly. For now.

choices.text: Hand the money to the LGA chairman 'for supervision'
choices.result: The money disappears into 'supervision'. The borehole never comes.

suspended.speaker: State Coordinator
suspended.text: The State Coordinator summons you. "You will be queried, and your allowance stopped for two months." The letter goes in your file forever.

choices.text: Accept the query and keep serving
choices.result: Two months of no allowance. You learn to cook beans fifteen ways.

choices.text: Lean on a 'connect' to make it disappear (₦30,000)
choices.result: The query is lost. Like a lot of things.

expelled.speaker: NYSC Director
expelled.text: "Your service is cancelled." Decamped. No certificate this year. You'll have to remobilise next year, if they let you.

choices.text: Remobilise and serve again next year

effects.log: NYSC service cancelled; remobilised the next year.

choices.result: A year later, white shorts again. The soldiers remember you.

choices.text: Forget NYSC and go straight to Abuja

effects.log: Decamped from NYSC and never went back.

choices.result: No certificate. Some doors close. Others never cared.

start.text: You are an adult in Abuja now. Rent is due weekly in this game (be grateful: real landlords want two years upfront). Your goal: financial freedom. Talent matters. Grind matters. Money and connections matter more.

dropout_intro.text: No certificate, no waiting. Some doors are closed to you: banks, ministries, big corporates. Others are wide open: business, trading, content, the road. And Slim's door is always open.

intro.text: Certificates in a nylon bag, CV printed at a business centre, and one good shirt. Walk the city, find work, build something. Open your phone for jobs, loans, contacts and the map.
